title: Somebody Else's List
subject: a woman who finds a stranger's handwritten shopping list in the pocket of a charity-shop wool coat, buys every item on it and cooks whatever that list was meant to become
caption: Sophisti-pop, late-80s British style. A singing fretless bass, muted jazz guitar chords with a chorus effect, soprano saxophone answering the vocal, a DX7-style electric piano, soft programmed drums with a live hi-hat. Glossy polished mix with gentle room reverb. Female alto, smooth and conversational, close-mic, light double-tracking on the chorus. 96 BPM, D major. Wistful, curious and quietly charmed. No trap drums, no autotune, no EDM drop, no rock distortion, no jazz scat.
lyrics:
[Intro - fretless bass and soprano sax]

[Verse 1]
Camel coat from the charity shop
Twelve pounds and it fit
Left-hand pocket, folded twice
A list in someone's script

[Pre-Chorus]
Leeks, two lemons, crème fraîche
Thyme, and don't forget the bread

[Chorus]
Somebody else's list
Somebody else's night
I'm filling up my basket
With the things you chose to write

[Verse 2]
Mussels, butter, half a pound
White wine, underlined
Who were you cooking for
With every word so kind

[Chorus]
Somebody else's list
Somebody else's plan
I'm stirring in the leeks now
Guessing who you are

[Bridge - sax solo]
Steam on the window
Mussels open one by one

[Chorus]
Somebody else's list
Somebody else's meal
I set a second plate down
Just to see how it would feel

[Outro - electric piano fade]
Fold it up, back in the pocket
Someone's dinner, kept
